newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EA-Generali to close Creditanstalt due diligence.
newsitem.headline: EA-Generali to close Creditanstalt due diligence.

text.p: A consortium of bidders for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt led by insurer EA-Generali will complete due diligence procedures on Monday, the Austrian government said on Friday.
It added a second bidder, whose identity remains unknown, had declined to take part in the due diligence process.
"As repeatedly stated, the submission of a final offer is not conditional upon taking part in the due diligence," the ministry said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
Final offers for the state's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt, the country's most traditional finance house, have to be submitted by December 16, the ministry added.
Finance Minister Viktor Klima has repeatedly said he wants to close the sale, Austria's longest-running privatisation project since World War Two, before the end of the year.

But on Thursday, Klima said it was unclear whether revenues from the sale could be realised in 1996 and indicated he may consider selling a stake in a second bank to make up for the possible shortfall.

Apart from Creditanstalt, the Republic of Austria owns postal savings bank PSK, which is to be turned into a joint stock company next year to prepare it for privatisation, and a 17 percent stake in Bank Austria, the country's largest bank. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
